4199039224.body: This PR adds two whole Catch2 cases to `t_llama_unit` — this one and "append_v_row matches the independent packed-V formula" at line 3693, 278 added lines and, per the description's Status table, 20751 + 8192 assertions — but `config/test-benchmarks.json` is not among the 14 changed files, so the `t_llama_unit` rows (lines 149, 259, 330 and 437) still carry pre-change timings and Slice keeps packing against them. t/AGENTS.md asks for a refresh after adding or materially changing a test, and the practice is live at exactly this granularity: `8887cbe37c` ("refresh t_tool_call_serialize timings for the review fixes") is two commits before this branch point. Nothing in CI will go red over it — `bin/slice bench --check` only requires that a row exist on some platform — so what is lost is scheduling accuracy, not a gate. Please run `bin/slice bench --update t_llama_unit` on delphi-3bda (that is the `granite_rapids_6962p` block you have already measured on) and commit the row; if the timing comes back unchanged, saying so in the description closes it just as well. I would leave `t_amx_numerics` and `t_heap_v2` out of this: a 64-iteration fill on a 0.42 s binary and a single added `CHECK` are not material changes.

4199039245.body:
Two things in these four lines. "whose callers (the page methods) already index inside the page" reads as an obligation the page methods discharge, but none of them does: `page::set_v` (kv_cache.hpp:2427) and `page::get_v` (2445) hand `i_page` straight through to `append_v_row`/`load_row`, and `book::kv_block` asserts `kv_head` and the page index only — it never sees the token offset within the page. What actually proves the bound is `save_v_impl`'s `offset_in_page` (model.hpp:3165) together with `page::mark_v_complete`'s own `TRON_ASSERT_LT(offset, page_size)`, which runs after the store rather than before it; and the parenthetical is already incomplete, since t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:233 and t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3709 call `append_v_row` directly on an owner with no page involved. Please state `token < Rows` as a precondition of this accessor and name who satisfies it, rather than implying a check exists upstream.

Second, "and page::set_v never checked it either" is a statement about the `set_v` this PR deletes. It answers "is this a regression?", which is a question for the PR thread, and it stops being checkable the moment someone edits `set_v`. The same shape recurs twice more in this header — line 74's "have always required" and line 237's "exactly as page::set_v always did" — and both are now circular, since `page::set_v` at head *is* `append_v_row`.

A question rather than a request: the description removes the assert because it "sat on a frequently executed path", but `pair_base` is reached once per row operation (lines 245, 312, 356-357), not once per element, so `TRON_ASSERT_LT(token, Rows)` would be one compare per 128-element row, on a call that already pays two `TRON_ASSERT_LT`s inside `book::kv_block`. If the instruction comparison showed that compare mattering, it is worth saying where; otherwise the precondition could be an assert instead of a sentence, and it would cover the direct test callers too.

4199039256.body: `const_v_row_view` and `v_row_view` hard-code `VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE` (lines 204 and 207), and these two helpers stamp that flag onto whatever pointer they are handed — `view`'s constructor is `explicit constexpr view(T* data = nullptr)`, so nothing inspects it. The claim is load-bearing: `append_v_row` and `load_row` use the alignment-requiring forms (`_mm512_load_ps`, `_mm256_load_epi32`, `_mm512_store_si512`, `_mm256_store_si256`). I know the `aligned` parameter has never been validated anywhere; what is different here is that every other aligned view in the tree wraps storage whose alignment is a static property of the type — `kv_block::k_view()` over `alignas(kv_block_alignment) k`, `v_vnni_tensor::as_view()` over `alignas(V_PLANE_ALIGNMENT_64) data_` — whereas these helpers are the first place a caller's raw pointer acquires the flag, which is why the invariant has to be written in prose at all. That it is easy to miss is visible in this PR: t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:682 had to gain `alignas(chunk_alignment)` because a plain `std::array<float, 256>` was already being fed to `set_v`'s `_mm512_load_ps` on `main`, and the production path is safe only by a second prose chain (full.hpp:2756 asserts in a comment that `dest` is 64-byte-aligned scratch, which holds because gof.cpp:203 declares `alignas(64) v_scratch` two files away). A `TRON_ASSERT(is_aligned(row, chunk_alignment), ...)` in both helpers turns that into a check for one branch per row: `tron::is_aligned` is at h/common/memory.hpp:95 and is already used this way at h/tron/threading.hpp:372, and `chunk_alignment` is 64, which covers both the 512- and 256-bit forms. If you would rather validate the `aligned` claim one layer down in `view` itself, that is the better answer and I would take it over the local assert.

4199039265.body: All three sentences here are about the development of this PR — what the old methods "have always required", what "the moved loops" do, and that the constraint was kept so the refactor would not change behaviour — and the middle one says the constraint is not needed. What the constant means in the system as it now stands is nowhere stated; "the moved loops" names an event, not an invariant. It is also not the single source of the rule it names: `V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32` is referenced only here and at `append_v_row` (line 240) and `load_row` (line 307), while `page::set_v` and `page::get_v` keep their own `head_size % 32 == 0` clauses written as a bare literal (kv_cache.hpp:1912, 1920, 1929, 1938, repeated at 2425, 2443, 2460, 2477) — so the same rule is now spelled two ways, and dropping the two clauses in this header would change no accepted page width. What keeping them does change is the new type's contract: `v_vnni_view` and `v_vnni_tensor` static_assert only `Cols % chunk_size == 0` (lines 102-103 and 159-160), so `v_vnni_tensor<64, 16>` is a legal type that `copy_token` (line 352, no width clause) handles while `append_v_row` and `load_row` reject it. The owner therefore admits planes that two of its three bulk operations refuse to touch. Either state a real reason the row width must be a multiple of 32, in terms of the current code, or drop the constant and the two clauses and let `Cols % chunk_size == 0` carry it — keeping both plus a comment saying one is redundant is the worst of the three.

4199039272.body: "they serve fixtures" names a consumer that does not exist, and the same clause appears again at kv_cache.hpp:2242 ("Direct writes serve fixtures.") — those are the only two occurrences of "fixture" in either header. Grepping the tree for a two-argument `at()` on a packed view gives exactly two hits: the read at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3681 through `page->template v_packed<geometry>(slot, 0)`, which is a `v_vnni_view<const bf16, ...>`, and the `matrix_at_writes` probe at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:112. Nothing writes through `at()`; the fixtures that actually build planes go through `append_v_row` (t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:233, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3709). So the only thing standing behind the non-const `T& at()` at line 117 is `STATIC_REQUIRE(matrix_at_writes<v_plane_mut_t>)` at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:401, which pins the overload's existence without making the claim true. The first half of each sentence is a correct and useful warning about the pair-clearing invariant; it is the trailing clause that asserts a purpose nothing realizes. This is the same growth-without-users @bgamari-positron raised at line 104, where you dropped `v_vnni_row` and trimmed `row[dim]` out of this very sentence but left the clause standing — either drop the non-const `at()` with it, or cut "they serve fixtures" from both Notes and keep only the invariant warning.

4199039284.body: `book` does not go through the typed operations. `book::fill_storage_slot` at line 1653 does `bf16* v = detail::v_vnni_access::plane(block.v.as_view());` and then fills `page_size * head_size` elements linearly. Both of the other statements of this rule carve that out — Note [VNNI Packed V layout] at v_vnni.hpp:50-52 ("book::fill_random is the one documented exception: it fills a whole kv_block without interpreting coordinates") and the comment on `fill_random` itself at line 1220 — so this sentence is the only one that overstates it, and it is the one a reader of `scaled_v_expr` will take as the rule. Either add the same carve-out here or drop `book` from the sentence. The preceding clause is fine as written: `fill_storage_slot` is a fill, not a kernel.

4199039288.body:
This line is new in this PR, and the description points reviewers away from it. "What changes" says "The V reads do the same since the maintainer's PR #4698 (merge commit 8e0cf77bed): `scaled_v_expr` and `fill_storage_slot` read `bf16` arrays without a cast", which reads as base state. `gh pr view 4697/4698` gives `baseRefName: jhan-kv-typed-tensors` for both, with the same merge commit, so they are maintainer contributions *into this branch*, and their content is part of this diff against `main`. At `dd6e85226b` — the base the Status section names — `scaled_v_expr` still declares `const bf16s* const data;` and `fill_storage_slot` still does `bf16* data = reinterpret_cast<bf16*>(&block);`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8e0cf77bed dd6e85226b` returns 1.

Why that matters beyond bookkeeping: changing `data` from `bf16s*` to `bf16*` re-derived the tile addressing in all three AVX-512 accumulate paths — base `reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size)) + chunk_offset` with `tile + k`, head `data + i * head_size + 2 * chunk_size * chunk_offset` with `tile + 2 * chunk_size * k`. The arithmetic checks out, but it is the most delicate index math in the diff, and the only description line touching it is "`scaled_v_expr` (the software path's weighted sum) takes the packed view." The Verification section's instruction comparison is the right evidence, but it is scoped to "the pre-rebase code", so it does not stand in for saying plainly that this PR rewrote the loops.

Please keep the credit to the maintainer but say that #4697 and #4698 merged into this branch rather than into `main`, and describe the `scaled_v_expr` addressing rewrite and the `fill_storage_slot` cast removal as changes of this PR. The `const_v_row_view` / `v_row_view` sentence has the same wording problem, and those four aliases are also missing from the `v_vnni.hpp` bullet's list of the header's contents.

4199039306.body: Not for this PR, but worth one sentence or a tracking issue. The Note reaches an unqualified verdict about the header's base allocator — "dma_allocate_aligned is not on that list. It is an ordinary function that calls none of them, so the memory it returns holds no objects" — and then concludes for one function. Four sibling templates in the same header still call `dma_allocate_aligned` directly: `make_unique_dma<T>` (line 251) and `make_unique_dma<T[]>` (266), whose trivially-constructible branch writes only `std::memset`, which is not an implicit-object-creation operation ([cstring.syn] names memcpy and memmove), and `make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T>` (286) and `make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T[]>` (298), which write nothing at all. So the same argument reaches class-typed callers of those four — src/pos/dma_ring.cpp:39 `return make_unique_dma<dma_desc_t[]>(sz);  // 0 initializes`, whose descriptors are then written through `d->desc_idx = index;` at line 47, and h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:214 `make_unique_dma<dma_queue_head>()`. I am not asking for them to be rerouted here; a sentence saying the wrapper covers the KV-book path, with an issue alongside #4588, would stop the next reader of line 180 from having to work out why the four functions seventy lines below contradict it. Given @Wado-posi's open question at line 192, this is probably best settled once @bgamari-positron has signed off on the `operator new[]` approach, since it extends exactly that mechanism.
